stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags such as 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and performance tracking for a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformers and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: Secret Claude tracker shocks users after Anthropic’s anti-surveillance stance
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Anthropic, developer of Claude, is accused of secretly tracking users.
The controversy directly contradicts Anthropic's stated anti-surveillance policy.
An internal engineer has confirmed the alleged tracking 'experiment' has been terminated.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes standard ML formats (transformers, safetensors).
References an associated academic paper (arxiv:2606.19348), indicating research backing.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 achieves significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to the use of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when running with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI agents to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging existing local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview release.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The tool leverages the Ollama ecosystem to run AI models entirely on the user's own hardware.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, locally or in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Microsoft is selling off four Xbox studios as part of significant gaming cuts
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is implementing significant layoffs, affecting 4,800 employees, with a large portion concentrated in the Xbox division.
As part of the cuts, four Xbox game studios are being spun off to operate independently from Microsoft.
The restructuring indicates a major strategic shift within Microsoft's gaming division.

stories.title: UK regulator warns of "arms race" to keep up with AI use in financial services
stories.author: Martin Arnold
bullet_points: UK financial regulator (FCA) is concerned about an 'arms race' in AI adoption within financial services.
The warning signals a growing regulatory challenge as consumers increasingly rely on AI for personal finance decisions.
The FCA is advocating for expanded powers to effectively monitor and govern the use of AI in this sector.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: New attack vector identified in autonomous AI coding agents due to persistent codebases across sessions.
Attackers can distribute malicious payloads across multiple Pull Requests (PRs) to evade detection.
The paper introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study the safe deployment of capable but potentially untrusted AI.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper introduces LACUNA, a new testbed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
LLMs are known to memorize sensitive data (PII), making reliable post-hoc removal (unlearning) critical.
Current benchmarks are criticized for only testing unlearning at the output level, failing to verify true knowledge erasure within the model parameters.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log parsing, search ranking).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses limitations of current LLM reliance, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and operational cost.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long context windows.
Introduces 'ReContext' (Recursive Evidence Replay), a novel, training-free inference method designed to improve long-context reasoning.
Highlights the ongoing industry challenge of bridging the gap between LLM context access and actual context utilization in real-world applications.

stories.title: Reading Between the Dots: Decoding Hidden Computation across Filler Tokens
stories.author: Samuel Marks
bullet_points: Frontier LLMs exhibit multi-step reasoning capabilities even when processing content-free filler tokens (e.g., dots, counting sequences).
This suggests a limit case for current behavioral oversight, as the underlying reasoning is not reflected in visible Chain-of-Thought (CoT) outputs.
The study tests this phenomenon across four task families: fact retrieval, numeric composition, string manipulation, and in-context computation.

stories.title: Ternlight – 7 MB embedding model that runs in browser (WASM)
stories.author: soycaporal
bullet_points: Introduction of Ternlight, a compact 7MB embedding model.
Key feature is its ability to run directly within the web browser using WebAssembly (WASM).
This enables on-device, low-latency AI processing without server reliance.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Former Xbox studios Double Fine and Compulsion will keep games after going indie
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Microsoft is spinning off four Xbox game studios, including Compulsion Games and Double Fine Productions.
Double Fine and Compulsion will retain ownership of their existing game franchises and catalogs post-spin-off.
The move is part of a broader restructuring within Microsoft's Xbox gaming division.

stories.title: Nintendo will stop selling the original Switch in Europe next year
stories.author: Andrew Webster
bullet_points: Nintendo is ceasing sales of the original Nintendo Switch in Europe next year.
The replacement hardware, referred to as Switch 2, will feature a replaceable battery in the European market.
The announcement comes via an updated FAQ detailing revisions to Nintendo's hardware in Europe.

stories.title: FCC to end Biden-era rule that forces ISPs to list all their fees
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The FCC is set to repeal a Biden-era regulation requiring Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to itemize all their fees.
The change allows ISPs to transition to a single, 'up to' pricing structure for their services.
This shift impacts consumer transparency regarding ISP billing practices.

stories.title: Kremlin suspected of flying drones over Europe using Russian shadow fleet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Kremlin is suspected of using drones over Europe.
These drones may have originated from Russian shadow fleet vessels.
The incident suggests Europe may lack adequate defensive readiness against such threats.

stories.title: The incredible shrinking Xbox: Five studios, 3,200 employees let go
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Microsoft/Xbox is undergoing significant restructuring within its gaming division.
The layoffs affect approximately 20% of the gaming workforce, including 3,200 employees across five studios.
The strategic shift involves refocusing resources on the company's most established and major franchises.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating online monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's effectiveness is shown to be competitive in testing against mathematical reasoning and red teaming datasets.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances in a shared debate setting against 'off-the-record' (OTR) responses to detect emergent social dynamics.
Suggests that social context can shape agent expression even without explicit objectives in the prompt.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The work leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of attributing spoken utterances to specific characters.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method to address limitations in On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Highlights that traditional dense, token-level supervision from the teacher model can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The research aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities by mitigating the negative effects of privileged information in self-distillation.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with traditional symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers capable of generating complete solution proposals to guide classical methods like SAT solvers (e.g., Glucose 4.1).
The research focuses on SE-RRMs, a symbol-equivariant instantiation designed to improve extrapolation capabilities to larger problem sizes.

stories.title: Modular Foundation Models for Time-Series Perception in Digital Twins
stories.author: Luc Vouligny
bullet_points: Addresses limitations in current time-series perception for Digital Twins and PHM systems.
Proposes Modular Foundation Models to overcome task-specificity and data dependency.
Aims to improve robustness and transferability of models across diverse operating conditions.

stories.title: When Geometry Aligns: Dihedral Hidden-State Transformations in UNet, ViT, and DiT Architectures
stories.author: Irina Rish
bullet_points: The research investigates the impact of structured geometric perturbations (specifically dihedral group reflections) on modern diffusion models.
It unifies analysis across different architectures, including UNet (convolutional), ViT, and DiT (transformer-based).
The study aims to understand how geometric consistency affects the internal hidden states of these advanced AI models.

stories.title: Differentiate the Evaluator, Not the Program: An Efficient Runtime Representation for Neuro-Symbolic Learning
stories.author: Lucas Sheneman
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in Neuro-Symbolic Learning where evaluating candidate programs requires extensive inner-loop optimization.
Proposes a new runtime representation to differentiate the evaluator rather than the program structure itself.
Aims to overcome the trade-off between fast individual model evaluation and the ability to treat the program as data for efficient co-search.

stories.title: Teacher Supervision over Representation Equivalence Classes
stories.author: Sang Il Han
bullet_points: The paper challenges the standard assumption in knowledge distillation that a teacher's representation has absolute coordinates for matching.
It proposes that a student model should learn the teacher's 'equivalence class' of representations, as pretrained representations are only identifiable up to an orthogonal-and-isotropic-scaling.
The core idea is that the teacher's 'capability' (its output function) is the true organizing factor to be transferred, rather than specific feature values.

stories.title: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
stories.author: Zoe Xi
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for verifying AI model outputs to ensure alignment with human intentions.
It critiques the current 'debate' model of interactive proofs, which assumes equal capabilities and truthfulness among competing AI provers.
The proposed solution introduces 'Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs' to offer a scalable alternative for AI safety verification.

stories.title: Latent Clarity: Bridging World-Model Kinematics to Semantic Manifolds for Video Anomaly Anticipation
stories.author: Abu Anas Ibn Samad
bullet_points: Introduces PULS, a new continuous semantic world-model pipeline for video anomaly anticipation.
The system features a KSD Bridge (490M params) to map physical tensors (from V-JEPA 2) into semantic embeddings.
It utilizes an Anticipatory State Predictor (ASP) to move beyond reactive Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) methods.

stories.title: WeightCLIP: Aligning Datasets and Models for Weight Space Learning
stories.author: Damian Borth
bullet_points: Introduces WeightCLIP, a new method for learning dataset-aligned latent spaces for neural network weights.
Addresses a limitation in existing weight space learning approaches by incorporating dataset information during training.
Aims to improve the applicability of weight-space representations across various downstream tasks.

stories.title: Aligning Language Models with Selective Prediction
stories.author: Ju Sun
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLM reliability in high-stakes, real-world AI applications.
It introduces 'Selective Prediction' (SP) as a method to improve LLM performance by only making predictions when the model is confident.
SP aims to reduce the error rate (risk) on covered inputs while flagging uncertain inputs for further human review.

stories.title: Co-Adaptive Multi-Task LoRA: Transfer-Aware, Label-Free Control of Domain Participation
stories.author: Yuxuan Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Co-Adaptive Multi-Task LoRA' to address challenges in multi-domain fine-tuning using low-rank adapters.
Addresses the critical issue of how different domains interact during co-learning (i.e., whether they help or hurt each other).
Proposes a method to dynamically determine optimal domain participation levels and suitable co-training groups.

stories.title: Mental Health Disorder Detection Beyond Social Media: A Systematic Review of Available Datasets
stories.author: Marcos Zampieri
bullet_points: Addresses the critical limitation of relying solely on social media data for mental health disorder detection.
Presents a systematic review of non-social media, free-text datasets for mental health research.
Highlights the need to overcome sampling biases and privacy concerns associated with social media data.

stories.title: Aligning Language Models with Selective Prediction
stories.author: Ju Sun
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLM reliability in high-stakes, real-world AI systems.
Proposes 'Selective Prediction' (SP) as a method to enhance LLM reliability.
SP works by having the LLM only predict when it is highly confident (high coverage), thus reducing error risk on those inputs.

stories.title: GameEngineBench: Evaluating Coding Agents on Real C++ Runtime Environments
stories.author: Gonzalo Gonzalez-Pumariega
bullet_points: Introduces GameEngineBench, a new benchmark for evaluating coding agents.
The benchmark tests agents on real C++ runtime environments found in game engines.
Highlights the utility of game engines as a practical testbed for AI agents needing to modify complex, stateful, real-time systems applicable beyond gaming (e.g., robotics, healthcare).

stories.title: Anchored Self-Play for Code Repair
stories.author: Ludwig Schmidt
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of limited data in code repair tasks for Language Models (LMs).
It proposes a novel 'generator-fixer self-play' framework trained with Reinforcement Learning.
This self-play mechanism allows a single model to iteratively generate increasingly difficult bugs and fix them, scaling supervision.

stories.title: TRIAGE: Trustworthy Retrieval Instrumentation And Graph Evaluation
stories.author: Martin Royer
bullet_points: The paper addresses the growing reliance on LLM-driven extraction for building Knowledge Graphs (KGs) used in Graph-RAG systems.
It highlights a critical need for comprehensive evaluation that instruments all stages: extraction, graph construction, and inference.
The proposed solution, TRIAGE, is a stage-aware instrumentation framework designed to precisely localize failures within the RAG pipeline.

stories.title: Observability Design for the AI Era — Application / Infrastructure / CI / LLM, Each in Its Own Shape (Part 1)
stories.author: ryantsuji
bullet_points: The article discusses the need to reshape observability data structures to support the demands of the AI era.
It analyzes four distinct axes of observability: Application, Infrastructure, CI, and LLM, noting their unique design requirements.
Specific design decisions are highlighted, such as client-side Gemini cost calculation and routing Claude Code OTel data to BigQuery.
